To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of the dermoscoping criteria blue-black sign, blue-white veil, pigment network, and pseudopods or white streaks is helpful in the diagnosis of seborrheich keratosis–similar melanoma, despite the presence in the lesion of other seborrheoch keratosis features.
dermoscopy can be helpful for diagnosing difficult melanomas that clinically resemble seborrheich keratosis.

dermoscopically seborrheich keratosis-like melanomas have a high frequency of melanocytic criteria (eg, blue-white veil, blue-black sign) and a low frequency of nonmelanocytic criteria (eg, yellowish keratin, milia-like cyst) and can be diagnosed with high accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and reliable method of diagnosis of skin lesions.
the study of the dermoscopes of melanomas that mimic seborrhea keratosis.
the identification of melanoma cases that clinically mimic sebornrheic keratoses, and that are often dermoscopically difficult to diagnose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a lesion that clinically resembles a seborrheie keratosis, and has the blue-black sign and/or a pigment network, pseudospods, and/or a blue-white veil, should be considered as a melanoma.
the presence of any one of these criteria is sufficient for a correct diagnosis of melanoma, and that the presence of 2 or more of these criteria is strongly suggestive of melanoma.
the blue-white veil, the blue-black sign and/or the presence of a pigment network are the main clues for diagnosing SK-like malignant melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, although SK-like melanomas can show dermoscopic clues of malignancy, their presence does not guarantee a melanoma diagnosis, and a careful evaluation of all criteria is necessary to avoid misdiagnosis.
, in a case with clinical suspicion of SK, the absence of the blue-black dermoscopic sign, pigment network and/or pseudopods or blue-white veil should raise suspicion for melanoma.

dermoscopic clues for the correct diagnosis of seborrheich keratosis–mimicking melanomas are: 1) the presence of blue-black sign, 2) the presence of a pigment network, 3) the presence of pseudopods or/and streaks, and 4) the presence of the so-called “blue-white veil”.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the aforementioned dermoscopic criteria, even in the presence of hyperkeratosis, fissures and ridge, comedo-like openings, or milia-like cyst, should raise concern of melanoma.
, even when a lesion shows some dermoscopic signs of SK, it is important to consider a differential diagnosis of melanoma.
dermoscopically suspicious lesions should be biopsied, even if they have some features of SK.
